blocks.text: This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) details the comprehensive measures and advanced technologies implemented by Indutch Composites Technology Pvt Ltd. to prevent and mitigate the emission of atmospheric pollutants, environmental nuisances such as noise, odor, vibration, road wear, and light pollution, and to ensure strict compliance with all applicable environmental regulations and standards, fostering sustainability.

This SOP applies to all employees, contractors, and personnel involved in facility operations, production, maintenance, and management across all Indutch Composites Technology Pvt. Ltd. sites. It specifically covers the Environment, Health & Safety (EHS) Department, which is responsible for monitoring and controlling air quality, in collaboration with the Production, Maintenance, and Compliance Departments to ensure adherence to environmental regulations and sustainability standards.

sections.title: Measures for Preventing Emissions of Atmospheric Pollutants and Other Environmental Nuisances

body.text:
Indutch utilizes advanced continuous emission monitoring systems (CEMS) to track pollutants such as CO2, NOx, and SO2 in real-time, ensuring compliance with environmental regulations.
The data collected by CEMS is analyzed continuously to detect any deviations from permissible limits, enabling prompt corrective actions to minimize environmental impact.
CEMS operations are subject to continuous monitoring by a third-party certified agency to ensure data accuracy and reliability.
Bi-monthly ambient air monitoring which includes (PM10, PM2.5, SO2, NOx) is conducted by certified third-party agencies to assess the overall air quality impact of our operations on the surrounding environment, with having alternatively designated locations for this monitoring.
Equipment Maintenance: Routine inspections and preventive maintenance schedules are in place for all critical equipment to prevent leaks and malfunctions.
Employee Training: Comprehensive training programs are conducted for employees on environmental policies, spill prevention, and emergency response procedures.

Noise Barriers: Installation of sound barriers around high-decibel equipment, such as compressors and generators, to reduce noise pollution.
Acoustic Insulation: Soundproofing materials are used in building construction to minimize noise transmission.
Operational Schedules: Noisy operations are scheduled during daytime hours to limit disturbances during the night.
Regular Noise Monitoring: We conduct noise monitoring at highly noisy areas every week to assess and manage sound levels effectively.

Activated Carbon Filters: These highly effective filtration systems are strategically installed in exhaust systems to efficiently absorb and neutralize a wide range of odorous compounds emitted during various manufacturing processes.
Biofilters: These specialized systems are specifically designed to treat air streams containing organic compounds that are known to cause unpleasant odors, utilizing biological agents to break down and eliminate odorous molecules effectively.
Material Handling: All materials known to cause odors are meticulously stored in securely sealed containers and carefully handled within well-ventilated areas to ensure minimal emission of odorous compounds into the environment.

The industrial centrifuge is fitted with vibration dampers to effectively reduce mechanical vibrations, thereby enhancing its operational stability and longevity.
Regular Monitoring: Vibration sensors are strategically placed throughout the equipment to continuously monitor and analyze vibration levels in real-time. This proactive approach helps in promptly identifying any deviations from normal operating conditions.
Scheduled Maintenance: A comprehensive maintenance schedule includes regular inspections and adjustments of vibration dampers and sensors. This ensures optimal performance and early detection of potential issues before they escalate.
Data Analysis: Collected vibration data is analyzed using advanced software tools to gain insights into equipment performance trends and to facilitate predictive maintenance strategies. This data-driven approach improves overall reliability and reduces downtime.

Directional Lighting: Installation of shielded lighting fixtures with advanced designs to minimize light spillage and glare.
Automatic Controls: Use of motion sensors and intelligent timers to ensure lights are only on when necessary.
Energy Efficiency: Implementing LED technology and other efficient measures for reduced energy consumption and environmental impact.

sections.title: Technologies Implemented to Mitigate Emissions of Dust and Particulate Matter (PM)

body.text:
Dust Suppression Systems: Water sprays and misting systems are strategically deployed to suppress dust emissions effectively during various stages of material handling and processing operations.
HEPA Filters: High-efficiency particulate air filters are meticulously installed within ventilation systems to effectively capture airborne dust, pollen, and other particulate matter, ensuring cleaner and safer indoor air quality.
Enclosures: Processes that generate dust, such as grinding and sanding, are carefully enclosed within robust structures to fully contain particulates and prevent their dispersion into the surrounding environment.

Regular Cleaning: Work areas are meticulously cleaned using advanced industrial vacuum systems to effectively minimize dust accumulation.
Proper Storage: Dust-producing materials are securely stored in tightly closed containers to prevent any dispersion into the air.

sections.title: Technologies Implemented to Mitigate Emissions of VOC, SO2, NOx, and Heavy Metals

body.text:
Activated Carbon Filters: These are integrated into industrial exhaust systems to efficiently capture and neutralize volatile organic compounds (VOCs), thereby reducing their atmospheric release.
Thermal Oxidizers: High-efficiency thermal oxidizers are employed to convert volatile organic compounds (VOCs) into environmentally benign by-products such as CO2 and water vapor through controlled high-temperature combustion processes.
Low-VOC Materials: Our manufacturing processes prioritize the use of low-VOC paints, adhesives, and solvents to minimize emissions and enhance environmental sustainability.

Flue Gas Desulfurization (FGD): Wet and dry FGD systems are implemented to effectively remove sulfur dioxide (SO2) from exhaust gases, ensuring compliance with stringent emission regulations.
Low-Sulfur Fuels: We utilize low-sulfur raw materials and fuels across our operations to significantly reduce the emission of sulfur dioxide (SO2) at its source.

Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR): Our facilities employ SCR technology to efficiently reduce nitrogen oxides (NOx) in flue gases by injecting a reagent like ammonia and passing the gases through a catalyst, ensuring optimal emission control.
Combustion Optimization: We optimize combustion processes by precisely controlling temperature and air-fuel ratios, thereby minimizing the formation of nitrogen oxides (NOx) during industrial operations.

Electrostatic Precipitators (ESP): We utilize advanced ESP systems to capture heavy metal particulates from exhaust gases using electrostatic charges, ensuring compliance with environmental standards.
Fabric Filters: Our operations incorporate fabric filters (baghouses) to effectively trap heavy metals and other particulates from industrial emissions, promoting cleaner air quality in surrounding environments.

Soundproof Enclosures: We implement soundproof enclosures around noise-generating equipment such as air compressors and vacuum pumps, using specialized materials to effectively mitigate noise emissions.
Quieter Machinery: Our facility invests in advanced machinery and equipment designed with integrated noise reduction features, ensuring quieter operations and improved workplace acoustic environments.
Noise Monitoring Systems: Continuous noise monitoring systems are employed to meticulously track and manage noise levels across our operations, ensuring strict adherence to regulatory requirements and maintaining a harmonious relationship with surrounding communities.

Daytime Operations: We schedule noisy operations exclusively during daytime hours to minimize the impact on nearby communities and residential areas.
Maintenance and Lubrication: Rigorous maintenance protocols are implemented, including regular lubrication of machinery components, to effectively reduce noise emissions caused by friction and wear, thereby promoting a quieter operational environment.

Staggered Work Hours: Implementing flexible work schedules to reduce peak traffic congestion by staggering employee arrival and departure times, thus minimizing the impact of commuting on local traffic flow.
Coordination with Authorities: Collaborating closely with local authorities to enhance road infrastructure and implement effective traffic management strategies around our company's facilities, ensuring smoother traffic flow and improved safety.

Advanced Planning: Leveraging advanced logistics and route planning software to optimize delivery and transport routes, effectively reducing travel distances and congestion while enhancing efficiency in our supply chain operations.
Employee Transportation: Actively promoting sustainable transportation options such as carpooling, offering company-provided shuttles, and encouraging the use of public transportation among employees, thereby reducing individual vehicle trips to and from our facilities.

Off-Peak Deliveries: Strategically scheduling deliveries during off-peak hours to minimize disruption to local traffic patterns and reduce congestion during peak commuting times.
Supplier Coordination: Collaborating closely with suppliers to synchronize delivery schedules with our traffic management strategies, ensuring that deliveries are timed to minimize their impact on local traffic conditions and optimize logistical efficiency.

narrative.text:
Regular Monitoring and Evaluation

Quarterly Assessments: Indutch conducts quarterly assessments to track progress towards air emission control goals. This includes evaluating emission levels, equipment maintenance activities, and process improvements.
Data Analysis: Data on emission levels, maintenance activities, and process optimizations are systematically analyzed to ensure ongoing compliance and continuous enhancement of air quality.
Reporting: The Environmental Manager at Indutch prepares detailed reports summarizing findings from quarterly assessments. These reports undergo review by senior management to inform strategic decision-making.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Tracking

Emission Levels: Indutch monitors and reports on key performance indicators related to the reduction of PM, VOCs, NOx, and SOx emissions, demonstrating commitment to environmental stewardship.
Maintenance Activities: The effectiveness of maintenance activities conducted on equipment is systematically tracked to ensure optimal performance and regulatory compliance.
Control Measures Efficiency: Indutch assesses the efficiency of dust and particulate matter control measures, noise reduction initiatives, and odor control strategies to uphold high environmental standards.
Deviation Management: Instances of deviations from air emission targets are promptly identified and corrective actions are implemented at Indutch. Actions taken are documented and reviewed during subsequent assessments to maintain rigorous compliance standards.

Employee Feedback and Engagement

Employee Engagement: Indutch actively engages employees in air emission control initiatives through regular training sessions, awareness programs, and recognition of their contributions to achieving air quality goals.
Feedback Collection: Regular feedback from employees on air emission control programs is collected through surveys, suggestion boxes, and monthly team meetings at Indutch.
Feedback Analysis: The Environmental Manager carefully reviews employee feedback and integrates valuable suggestions into the air emission control plan, ensuring continuous improvement and fostering a culture of environmental responsibility among employees.

Incident Reporting and Response

Incident Documentation: Indutch diligently documents all incidents involving unexpected releases of pollutants, including their causes, response actions taken, and outcomes. Records are meticulously maintained for at least five years.
Response Evaluation: Following each incident, Indutch conducts thorough evaluations to identify root causes and implements corrective actions swiftly to prevent recurrence. These evaluations are systematically reviewed during quarterly assessments to further strengthen incident response protocols.

sops.title: Sustainable Energy Management and Resource Optimization

blocks.text: This SOP outlines the advanced technical strategies and equipment implemented by Indutch Composites Technology Pvt. Ltd. to reduce overall energy consumption, enhance process efficiency, and minimize energy waste through effective heat retention and conversion. It also captures the deployment of waste heat utilization systems and dual-output energy units, contributing to the company's long-term sustainability roadmap.

This SOP applies to all technical departments, production areas, maintenance teams, infrastructure planners, and utility operators engaged in equipment upgrades, process optimization, and energy monitoring across all Indutch facilities.

body.text:
Routine internal energy audits and thermal imaging diagnostics identify energy-intensive zones and inefficient machinery.
Production-level benchmarking is carried out using specific energy consumption (SEC) metrics for each process line.

Intelligent HVAC Enhancements: Integration of High-Volume Low-Speed (HVLS) fans with PMSM motors reduces air-conditioning load by up to 40%.
Smart Lighting Systems: Motion-controlled and daylight-sensitive LED fixtures deployed across workspaces to eliminate idle load consumption.
IE3+ Motor Replacements: Obsolete motors across conveyors, mixers, and blowers are being upgraded to high-efficiency standards.
Inverter and Sensor-Based Cooling Units: Process-sensitive equipment is retrofitted with inverter compressors and smart thermostats.

PLC-Controlled Machines: Installed on heating systems, compressors, and curing stations to run time- and load-based schedules.
VFD-Driven Pumps and Mixers: Automatically adjust output based on load demand, reducing peak loads and enhancing motor lifespan.
Digital Meters: Installed for real-time analysis of voltage, current, power factor, and energy trends at the machine level.

Adoption of low-cure-temperature resin systems and closed-loop vacuum infusion reduces overall curing energy.
Energy load is reduced by replacing batch ovens with zoned heating solutions in mould curing cycles.

Installation of Air Handling Unit (AHU)-based HVAC systems in production and storage areas (160m x 30m size).
Maintains internal temperature in the range of 25–28°C for thermal consistency.
Reduces curing material defects and unplanned equipment downtime due to temperature fluctuations.
Enhances indoor energy efficiency by minimizing compressor overloads and external heat gains.

sections.title: Heat Recovery and Dual-Output Energy Systems

body.text:
25 mm NBR insulation sheets are applied beneath electrically heated composite moulds, limiting thermal transmittance to 1.373 W/m²K, and reducing heat loss by over 88%, as validated by ISO 12241.
Insulation reduces energy draw from PLC-based heating systems and improves temperature retention during curing downtime.

Recuperators and heat exchangers installed on high-temperature exhausts (from ovens, compressors, and vacuum systems) to recover lost thermal energy.
Recovered heat is redirected to preheat process water, resin tanks, or air streams used in drying and curing.

CHP units are integrated where consistent electric and thermal loads exist (e.g., curing, mould prep, office HVAC).
CHP units generate electricity while capturing waste heat for facility water heating and process use, achieving >75% efficiency.

All systems are interfaced with the plant's energy dashboard to measure real-time heat recovery efficiency and fuel-to-energy ratios.
Thermal insulation and heat capture systems follow stringent safety protocols and are verified every 6 months for integrity and performance.

blocks.text: This SOP is reviewed annually, or whenever necessary, to ensure alignment with legal requirements and industry best practices in energy efficiency and resource optimization.

sops.title: Green Material Substitution and Hazardous Substance Minimization

blocks.text: This SOP establishes Indutch’s commitment to environmental sustainability through the adoption of eco-friendly input materials, substitution of hazardous substances, and toxicity reduction in operations. It outlines process upgrades, material choices, and handling techniques used to reduce environmental and occupational health risks while improving product lifecycle impacts.

This SOP applies to the procurement team, production planning, R&D, composite moulding operations, chemical stores, and quality control units across all Indutch facilities where material usage and handling occur.

sections.title: Integration of Eco-Friendly and Bio-Based Input Materials

body.text:
Use of natural fiber reinforcements (e.g., flax, jute) in non-structural composite components to reduce carbon intensity.
Adoption of bio-resins and epoxy systems with >30% renewable carbon content for moulding and adhesive applications.
Replacement of petroleum-based waxes and mold-release agents with soy-based or water-soluble variants.
Procurement of biodegradable consumables, such as starch-based gloves, coveralls, and packing films for logistics.

Suppliers are evaluated annually for their compliance with REACH and RoHS directives.
Preference is given to vendors offering material Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs) or green chemistry certifications.

rows: Reduces plastic waste and landfill impact

sections.title: Use of Alternative, Less Hazardous Substances in Operations

body.text:
Use of low-VOC (volatile organic compound) coatings and water-based paints in tool identification, protective coatings, and touch-up jobs.
Banned the use of lead, chromium VI, and heavy-metal pigments from all internal coating jobs.

Switched to bio-based or water-borne adhesives in sandwich panel assembly and tack bonding.
Solvent cleaning systems are transitioned from acetone to bio-ester-based degreasers with low evaporation rates and minimal toxicity.

Use of vegetable oil-derived hydraulic fluids and mold lubricants, compliant with ISO 15380 standards for biodegradable products.
Oils used in rotary and vacuum systems are selected based on toxicity and aquatic impact profiles, avoiding halogenated and mineral-heavy options.
Indutch strictly prohibits the use of any Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs) as listed under the Stockholm Convention. These include but are not limited to:

Polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs)
Dioxins and furans
Organochlorine pesticides (e.g., DDT, aldrin, chlordane)
Polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDEs) used in flame retardants

sections.title: Reduction of Hazardous Substance Generation & Toxicity

body.text:
Transitioned several resin transfer operations from open-bath to closed-loop vacuum infusion, preventing operator exposure to fumes.
Implemented UV-cure resins in R&D for fast-setting applications with minimal solvent off-gassing.
Air handling units in critical zones are fitted with HEPA + activated carbon filters to trap airborne chemical compounds.

Hazardous materials are stored in double-containment cabinets with ventilation and spill trays to avoid accidental mixing or leaks.
Color-coded labelling system with GHS pictograms helps employees immediately recognize and handle materials safely.

Batch-wise material planning and automated resin mixing systems are used to avoid overuse or wastage of reactive chemicals.
Pre-preg composite solutions with embedded catalysts reduce the need for on-site chemical activators, lowering cumulative toxicity.

blocks.text:
This SOP is annually reviewed to ensure alignment with legal requirements and industry best practices in green chemistry, material safety, and hazardous substance management.
Any updates or revisions to the SOP are communicated promptly to all employees and relevant stakeholders through training sessions, internal bulletins, and version-controlled documentation.

sops.title: Internal Waste Minimization and Waste Stream Mapping
sops.department: Environment, Health & Safety (EHS) and Compliance Departments

blocks.text: This SOP defines the processes and practices adopted by Indutch Composites Technology Pvt Ltd to minimize internal waste generation through reuse, recovery, and repurposing strategies, and to enhance operational waste management through comprehensive waste stream mapping. It also includes tracking, segregation, and evaluation practices to promote resource efficiency and circular economy alignment.

This SOP applies to all employees, contractors, and personnel involved in production, maintenance, warehouse operations, office administration, and waste management activities across all Indutch Composites Technology Pvt. Ltd. facilities. It specifically covers the Environment, Health & Safety (EHS) and Compliance Departments, which are responsible for monitoring waste minimization practices, in coordination with Production, Maintenance, Warehouse, and Administration teams to ensure effective waste stream mapping and resource efficiency.

sections.title: Internal Waste Minimization Through Reuse, Recovery, and Repurposing

substeps.text: Reuse of composite cut-off materials from blade moulding processes for sample testing, R&D prototypes, and non-critical parts.
Recovery of resin containers, spools, wooden crates, and drums, which are cleaned and reused for internal logistics or returned to vendors.
Reuse of foam blocks and packaging inserts during inter-unit component movement to minimize virgin packaging use.
Internal collection and reuse of steel frames, trolleys, and racks for in-house fabrication and refurbishing of shopfloor equipment.
Electronic equipment components (from CNC controllers, motor units, power tools) are harvested and reused as spares where safety permits.

sections.title: Strategic Enhancements for Waste Reduction and Resource Efficiency

body.text: Clearly labeled bins are placed across all production and office zones (color-coded as per waste type). QR-coded stickers on bins enable digital tracking of waste movement.
Waste management and segregation training is conducted quarterly. Cross-functional teams are encouraged to suggest new reuse/recovery ideas, with best ideas receiving recognition and rewards.

sops.title: Water Efficiency and Wastewater Control in Manufacturing

blocks.text: This SOP defines Indutch’s commitment to sustainable water management by implementing water-efficient cooling systems, minimizing water use in painting and cleaning, and establishing strict controls on wastewater from finishing operations. It also includes additional measures for recycling, monitoring, and treating process water to reduce environmental footprint.

This SOP applies to all departments and personnel involved in equipment cooling, surface treatment, component cleaning, and finishing operations, including maintenance, production, and facility engineering teams across all Indutch manufacturing locations.

body.text:
Replacement of traditional open-loop water-cooled chillers with air-cooled or hybrid cooling units that require minimal to no water consumption.
Use of closed-loop recirculating cooling systems with inline filtration and treatment, allowing cooling water to be reused multiple times without discharge.
Installation of dry cooling towers where operationally feasible, reducing dependency on water evaporation-based heat exchange.

Cooling demand is optimized through variable frequency drives (VFDs) and temperature automation to reduce unnecessary load on chillers.
Real-time temperature sensors and flow meters are integrated to prevent overcooling and identify water loss points quickly.
Cooling System Efficiency Summary

sections.title: Water Use Reduction in Painting and Cleaning

body.text:
Use of high-efficiency paint booths with low-pressure high-volume (LPHV) sprayers, reducing overspray and minimizing water washdown needs.
Application of dry-filter systems in spray areas instead of traditional water curtain booths.
All touch-up painting areas are equipped with non-aqueous wiping solvents instead of wet rinsing.

Adoption of multi-stage cleaning systems with recirculating wash/rinse tanks and periodic regeneration using chemical recovery units.
Implementation of automated, high-pressure low-flow jets for component washing instead of manual water jets.
Cleaning schedules are optimized to reduce frequency without compromising product quality.
Water Reduction in Surface Treatment

sections.title: Control of Wastewater in Finishing Operations

body.text: Finishing operations such as deburring, quenching, polishing, and sanding generate wastewater with oil residues, particulate metals, and chemical residues.

Installation of oil-water separators in deburring and quenching units to separate tramp oils before discharge.
Use of in-process filtration and settling tanks to remove suspended solids and recover reusable oils.
Wastewater is diverted to zero liquid discharge (ZLD) systems or effluent treatment plants (ETP) depending on location and regulatory requirement.

Shopfloor finishing zones are equipped with secondary containment trenches and spill protection bunds to avoid accidental discharge.
Wastewater quality is monitored weekly for COD/BOD/oil content prior to treatment or discharge.

Indutch maintains roof-based rainwater harvesting systems that recharge borewells and reduce freshwater dependency.
Collection tanks are equipped with first-flush filters and level sensors for maintenance control.

Training sessions on water-efficient practices are conducted quarterly for shopfloor and housekeeping teams.
Visual dashboards on shopfloor display real-time water consumption metrics to promote awareness.

narrative.text:
Daily logbooks and digital flow meters track water usage by process area.
KPIs include liters per unit produced, reuse ratio, % of water treated internally, and water savings.
Quarterly review of trends is done by the EHS & Maintenance teams to propose new savings projects.

blocks.text:
This SOP is annually reviewed to ensure alignment with emerging water conservation technologies and regulatory requirements under the Water Act, 1974.
Any updates or revisions to the SOP are communicated promptly to all employees and stakeholders via training and controlled document circulation.

sections.title: Ergonomic Risk Prevention and Repetitive Strain Injury (RSI) Management

Rotational work practices are adopted to reduce prolonged repetitive movements.
Tools and equipment are designed or selected to minimize strain on wrists, shoulders, and back.

Instructional posters and digital dashboards remind workers to take micro-breaks and maintain neutral posture.

Regular awareness workshops on mindfulness, stress management, and resilience-building.

This SOP applies to all Indutch teams involved in product design, engineering, manufacturing, testing, and after-sales support. It covers processes that impact product efficiency, durability, safe use, maintenance, and environmental performance.

sections.title: Guidance for Efficient Use, Storage, and Maintenance

substeps.text: Comprehensive product manuals provide instructions on efficient use to reduce unnecessary energy or resource consumption.
For chemical-based products, guidelines emphasize correct storage temperatures, ventilation requirements, and spill prevention methods.
Digital resources and QR-linked guides offer best practices on preventive maintenance to extend product lifespan.

MSDS documents include detailed guidance on hazards, storage conditions, personal protective equipment (PPE), first aid measures, and spill response.

Products are designed to consume less electricity, water, and consumables during operation.
Use of energy-efficient motors, LED systems, and lightweight composite materials reduces energy demand.
Equipment design includes optimized flow paths and low-drag surfaces to reduce operating loads.
Energy-saving curing technologies in composite processes.
Water-saving systems in cooling and washing operations.
Low-consumable designs that minimize reliance on inks, toners, or disposable filters.

sops.title: Sustainable Electrical and Electronic Product Design

blocks.text: This SOP defines Indutch’s approach to enhancing the sustainability of its electrical and electronic products by eliminating substances of concern, enabling efficient recovery and recycling, and designing products for safe disassembly, remanufacturing, and circular use. The objective is to minimize environmental impact, reduce hazardous waste, and support regulatory compliance with RoHS, WEEE, and similar global standards.

This SOP applies to all Indutch teams engaged in product design, engineering, procurement, manufacturing, testing, and end-of-life recovery programs. It is relevant for all electrical and electronic product lines and components produced or managed by Indutch.

sections.title: Guidance for Efficient Use, Storage, and Maintenance

body.text:
Indutch strictly avoids or minimizes the use of the following substances of concern:
Lead, mercury, cadmium, hexavalent chromium
Polybrominated biphenyls (PBB), Polybrominated diphenyl ethers (PBDE)
DEHP, BBP, DBP, DIBP (restricted phthalates)
Nickel, zinc, beryllium, yttrium, antimony trioxide
PVC and halogenated flame retardants
Where elimination is not yet technically feasible, substitution with eco-friendly alternatives is prioritized.

Procurement follows a restricted substance list (RSL) aligned with RoHS and REACH directives.
Suppliers must provide compliance declarations confirming products are free of restricted substances.
Internal audits and XRF testing are used to verify absence of restricted elements.

All electrical and electronic components are labeled with standardized recycling codes and material identifiers.
Hazardous or critical materials (batteries, capacitors, PCBs) carry special disposal instructions.

Indutch implements reverse logistics programs to take back end-of-life products for safe processing.

sections.title: Design for Circularity and End-of-Life Management

body.text:
Products are designed with modular components to allow easy removal and repair.
Use of standard fasteners instead of proprietary or permanent joining methods (e.g., rivets, glues).
Designs favor snap-fit joints, fewer screws, and detachable modules for faster disassembly.

Components are designed for remanufacturing and reuse, extending product lifecycles.
Materials are selected based on ease of recycling, low contamination risk, and high recovery yield.
Packaging and labeling support sorting of materials at end-of-life.

KPIs include % of RoHS-compliant parts, % of products designed for disassembly, and recovery rates of e-waste.

sops.title: ESG Due Diligence for Third Parties

blocks.text: This SOP establishes Indutch’s structured program for conducting ESG due diligence on all third parties, including suppliers, contractors, agents, and service providers. The program ensures that all third-party engagements align with Indutch’s sustainability commitments and regulatory obligations, while also mitigating risks related to environmental, social, governance, and ethical concerns.

This SOP applies to all third-party entities engaged by Indutch, including but not limited to suppliers, vendors, commission agents, brokers, distributors, contractors, customs brokers, consultants, and representatives. It covers all employees and teams involved in supplier management, procurement, compliance, and sustainability functions.

sections.title: Risk-Based Third-Party ESG Due Diligence Framework

body.text:
A risk-based approach is applied to assess third parties based on sector, geography, product category, and past compliance record.
Risk categories include: High Risk, Medium Risk, and Low Risk, with audit frequency and intensity adjusted accordingly.
